text:
Kimi K3's open weights drop tonight.

2.8 trillion parameters. The largest open-source model ever released. Kimi API Platform
Everyone is going to say "you can run it locally."

The honest version: you need a minimum of 8× H100 GPUs just to load it. A single RTX 4090 cannot run it even quantized. Explainx

The hype will be loud. The hardware reality will be quiet.

label: constraintedge-1m
name: Constraint Edge
text: That’s basically the AWS model: self-hosting is cheaper at high, steady utilization. Most companies would rather pay a premium for instant capacity, flexibility and no infrastructure burden. Running Kimi K3 internally could require roughly $1M+ of hardware before power, networking and an AI ops team.

label: circumjovial-100k
name: Circumjovial
text: They're only raising concerns about the frontier-level models, not lobbying to ban open weight models. Besides, Kimi K3 would take about $100,000 worth of hardware for someone to run at home. Nobody is gonna do that anyway so it's moot. There ARE real security concerns with a model as powerful as Kimi K3 being available to well-funded malicious adversaries. This is all rather overblown, and, ultimately, the letter itself means and obligates nothing.

label: cline-selfhost-savings
name: Cline
text:
Kimi costs ~3-12x cheaper than Fable, but how much more could you save hosting it yourself?

We ran the numbers on Cline’s production traffic, and the results:

~10% savings, 25%+ with time-of-day autoscaling (but this only works if over $500K/year of spend)

We predict self-hosting open weight models is going to become standard practice as businesses scale their token consumption with increased adoption, given the price and data sovereignty benefits.

And we’re excited to see Kimi K3 bring us closer to this future, enabling broader and more competitive access.

label: haider-correct-selfhost
name: Haider.
text:
i need to correct something:

i made it sound like an individual could realistically self-host kimi k3 today, which is clearly not true

what i meant to write was that large companies with serious infrastructure can afford to run models at this scale, and i know some people working at companies that already host very large models locally, but this is not practical for individual users

however, i expect that over the next 12–15 months, better quantization, memory efficiency, inference software, and cheaper hardware could make running models at this scale locally far more affordable and practical

once again, i apologize for the confusion
